review_method: Independent visual review of the original regional map pages and complete selected baseline groups, with independent private decoding of every selected fragment and original metadata. Public validation checks only included summaries and factual linkage.
counted_unit: Distinct logical inventory target IDs, not individual named rivers or verified reach names.

inherited_scope_continuity.supported_name_scope: The complete eastern basin corresponds at regional scale to water beneath the Lake part of the Sandfly Lake label. Its broad northern cap, western notch, eastern indentation and lower eastward arm taper into the southern tip. The full outline was compared with mapped water and surrounding shore. This supports generalized Sandfly Lake association for the selected feature, not equivalence with the entire named lake or extension of that name to connecting river water.

The entire north-south outline corresponds geographically to mapped water between Struga, Ohrid and Pogradec. Its broad northern cap, northeast shoulder, long east and west sides and rounded southern end were compared. Lake Ohrid is a low-confidence geographic naming candidate from literal wording within a partial conservation overlay, qualified by re-designate. Strong shape correspondence does not establish name coverage or naming authority for the complete selected water polygon. No supported whole-water identity or protected-site/water-boundary equivalence is assigned.

naming_scope_details.unassigned_region: Name coverage over the complete selected waterbody, including every source and baseline ring position.
naming_scope_details.follow_up_scope: Resolve independent lake-name authority and name coverage over the complete selected waterbody before promoting the Lake Ohrid candidate. Conservation-area wording is insufficient; no geometry repair is prescribed by this hold.

inherited_scope_continuity.supported_name_scope: The complete northern basin, indented western shore, elongated southwestern lobe, eastern side and southeastern projection correspond geographically to the large water east of Galicica. Prespa Lake is a low-confidence geographic naming candidate from the literal wording in Prespa Lake Monument of Nature over part of the cross-border water. Conservation-area wording does not establish name coverage or naming authority for the entire selected polygon. Great Prespa, exact named-water extent and protected-site/water-boundary equivalence remain unverified; no supported whole-water identity is assigned.

inherited_scope_continuity.supported_name_scope: The complete northeastern head, west-side indentation, east edge and long southwestern tail were compared with the separate southeastern water beneath the Prespa National Park (GR) overlay. No distinct waterbody label for that complete water was established. The park label and neighboring northern-lake designation do not establish a Small/Lesser Prespa name or extend the northern designation to this feature. Its whole-target name remains unassigned after full-outline review.

findings.follow_up_scope: No follow-up is required to complete the bounded representative-system assessment. Any separately authorized name application would require: Resolve the southern feeder name and reach-level name scope, including storage transitions and coastal/delta ending, before any per-reach or group scalar name application.
findings.supported_name_scope: The complete selected northern inland course, southeastward middle course, northward lower bend and southern tributary were considered against the directly labelled Burdekin channel and regional drainage pattern. Burdekin River is supported as a representative system identity. This does not assign Burdekin to the selected southern tributary, all headwater reaches, storage passages, coastal continuation or every rendered part.
limits: Direct channel labelling, surrounding coastline and the complete southward-then-coastward course support representative identity; the catchment title alone is not the basis.
The selected southern tributary is not given a specific river name. Nearby Cape and Bowen labels are contextual distinctions, not selected-fragment assignments.
The original publication is a regional assessment, not a formal naming-register decision or surveyed mouth map.
Original HydroRIVERS source-coordinate equality, exact source reach-to-rendered-part mapping and exact contemporary mouth are not verified.

confidence.basis: One government regional publication supplies direct channel wording and coarse whole-group geographic correspondence; it does not establish exact reach names or formal registry authority.

findings.supported_name_scope: The complete selected path runs from the southeastern inland extension through the long westward middle course and then northwest toward the Gulf. The directly labelled lower Gilbert channel and the distinct upstream Einasleigh corridor support Gilbert River as the representative system identity. The upper selected route is a coarse geographic association with Einasleigh; the exact transition and individual reach names are unassigned. The modeled mainstem role does not establish uniform Gilbert naming.
limits: The lower Gilbert and distinct Einasleigh labels must remain separate. No exact confluence, name transition or upstream headwater name is assigned.
A baseline mainstem role is a model property, not proof that every selected part has the same geographic name.

findings.supported_name_scope: The entire selected group includes the northern east-to-west modeled mainstem, its lower northwestward course, the long southern branch and the shorter northern tributary. Direct Mitchell labelling on the lower channel supports Mitchell River as the representative system identity. The upper modeled mainstem follows the regional Palmer corridor and the southern branch follows the Walsh corridor. These are geographic associations, not exact reach-name assignments. The shorter northern tributary, precise transitions and coastal continuation remain individually unnamed.
limits: Mitchell-Coleman is a regional catchment grouping, not a compound name assigned to this selected system.
Palmer and Walsh remain distinct regional channel names. The upper modeled mainstem is not uniformly named Mitchell, and the shorter northern tributary receives no name.

included_evidence_limit: Only public factual summaries, bibliography and included-file integrity are testable here. The omitted original maps, full selected paths, private decoder inputs and past visual judgments cannot be reproduced by public validation. Representative identity is not a uniform name for every reach or a product approval.
